P02-009.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.11.14 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, the strict word-event formula (one of the book's 39 strict-form onsets), opens an oracle addressed to the exiles rather than to the courtyard men of Ezek.11.1-11.13 — an addressee-class shift inside the vision, from the Jerusalem claimants (oshb:Ezek.11.15, which the WEB renders “This land has been given to us for a possession.” (web:Ezek.11.15)) to “your brothers… the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.11.15) in exile. The witness records a pe after MT 11:13 (single-witness), at the seam this unit opens on at 11:14. Close: oshb:Ezek.11.21 וְאֶל לֵ֧ב שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֛ם וְתוֹעֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם לִבָּ֣ם הֹלֵ֑ךְ דַּרְכָּם֙ בְּרֹאשָׁ֣ם נָתַ֔תִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה (one of the book's 81 utterance-close verses). The close seam is two-faced: the utterance signature ends 11:21 and the vision's return to the prophet opens at 11:22. The onset's far face is not: MT 11:13 ends on the prophet's own cry and carries no close-role formula, and the pe recorded after it corroborates the paragraph without supplying one. That one bare far face is the evidence this row's confidence reports. This embedded salvation oracle stands inside the still-open vision (the courtyard scene has not yet returned the prophet — that happens only at 11:22-25) but is bounded by its own onset and close formulae independent of the vision frame, so it is set as its own row rather than folded into 11:1-13 or 11:22-25.
P02-009.strongest_rejected_alternative: Holding 11:14-21 inside a single long 11:1-21 courtyard-and-oracle row, with the word-event at 11:14 disclosed only as internal texture, was weighed as an alternative reading. It was not taken because 11:14 is a strict word-event onset (not a bare transition) and the oracle's own addressee — the scattered exiles — differs from the courtyard men addressed in 11:1-13, which is enough of a class shift to justify treating it as its own formula-bounded row even while the wider vision frame stays open around it. A second rival sits inside this row and is weighed here as well: a seam at 11:16/11:17, and behind it a seam at 11:15/11:16. This witness records a samekh after MT 11:15 and another after MT 11:16 (single-witness), and because the witness enters each mark on the verse it stands after, both fall immediately before a verse that carries the long messenger formula כה אמר אדני יהוה — oshb:Ezek.11.16 and oshb:Ezek.11.17, two of that formula's 122 verses. Neither seam is licensed as a sub-onset, since a messenger formula opens one only if the people addressed change or the verse just before it finishes on a close-role formula. The addressee holds steady: the son-of-man address and the scattered exiles are named at 11:15 and nothing readdresses the oracle before 11:21. Nor does either preceding verse finish on a close-role formula — MEASURED on the pointed witness, MT 11:15 finishes לָ֥נוּ הִ֛יא נִתְּנָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ לְמוֹרָשָֽׁה (oshb:Ezek.11.15) and MT 11:16 finishes בָּאֲרָצ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אוּ שָֽׁם (oshb:Ezek.11.16), while in 11:16 and in 11:17 alike the messenger formula stands at the verse's head after לכן אמר rather than at its end. A mark alone cannot stand in for that verse-final formula, so the two samekhs are disclosed for the paragraph structure they corroborate within the row, and the row rests on its strict word-event onset at 11:14 and its verse-final utterance close at 11:21 (MEASURED: נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה closes MT 11:21; oshb:Ezek.11.21).
P02-009.device_notes: Filed under the salvation-oracle category on the restoration promise that is the unit's burden (gather-and-return is stated here: MEASURED at oshb:Ezek.11.17, the oracle both gathers and gives the land — the consonantal skeleton carries וקבצתי אתכם מן העמים ואספתי אתכם מן הארצות and ונתתי לכם את אדמת ישראל, which the WEB renders “I will gather you from the peoples, and assemble you out of the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.” (web:Ezek.11.17) — and the “one heart… heart of flesh” (web:Ezek.11.19) promise stands alongside it, so that filing rests on the device the unit actually carries); a one-sentence deviation is disclosed because the unit also carries a disputation-oracle color (the quoted Jerusalem claim at 11:15 is refuted before the promise is given), and the category is not read as free text beyond that single disclosure. No K/Q or paseq falls in this span, on the single-witness apparatus.

Close: oshb:Ezek.13.23 לָכֵ֗ן שָׁ֚וְא לֹ֣א תֶחֱזֶ֔ינָה וְקֶ֖סֶם לֹא תִקְסַ֣מְנָה ע֑וֹד וְהִצַּלְתִּ֤י אֶת עַמִּי֙ מִיֶּדְכֶ֔ן וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ן כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה ends “Then you will know that I am Yahweh.” (web:Ezek.13.23) in the second-feminine-plural form (וידעתן), a counted form of its own (sweep: 2 verses) that belongs to neither the 3mp-28 nor the 2mp-21 recognition class, though both of its verses are members of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), whose members are refrain-grade close evidence; a matching 2fp clause also closes the magic-bands sub-paragraph at oshb:Ezek.13.21. P02-020.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.14.12 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, a strict word-event formula, opens the Noah-Daniel-Job oracle on personal versus vicarious righteousness. P02-020.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at oshb:Ezek.14.20, where a pe falls after the fourth triad refrain (single-witness) and immediately before the oracle turns from the hypothetical four scourges to their explicit application to Jerusalem (14:21-23), is the standing rival, and it is weighed here rather than passed over. MT 14:21 opens with a messenger formula: MEASURED on this witness's consonantal skeleton, oshb:Ezek.14.21 begins כי כה אמר אדני יהוה, and that verse is among the 122 verses that carry the long messenger formula. What it opens is nonetheless a paragraph, not a sub-onset, since a messenger sub-onset is granted only where the addressee changes or where the verse just before it ENDS on a close-role formula, and neither condition is met. Nothing marks a new addressee at 14:21 — MEASURED, the son-of-man address falls at MT 14:3 and MT 14:13 and at no other verse of this chapter, chapter 14 carries no set-your-face verse at all, and 14:21 is not opened by 'and you, son of man' — so what turns there is the subject, from a hypothetical land to Jerusalem, and not the person addressed. As for the second condition, the utterance formula in MT 14:20 does NOT reach the verse end: MEASURED, נאם אדני יהוה sits at characters 29 through 41 of an 81-character skeleton, the first character counted as 1 and both ends included, and from there the oath's own content runs to the etnachta, with אם בן אם בת יצילו המה בצדקתם יצילו נפשם standing between that signature and the sof pasuq, its second clause independent after the major disjunctive. So the pe on MT 14:20 is entered as support for the rival it favours and for no more than that: this witness records the break after MT 14:20, a mark cannot supply the verse-final close-role formula that the second condition asks for, and paragraph evidence informs while every licensed driver outranks it. The row carries on to its own verse-final utterance close at oshb:Ezek.14.23.

Paseq at 14:21 is count-only, single-witness. oshb:Ezek.15.1 is cited above only as forward-side onset evidence for the seam; it is not a row here. Length disclosure: this row is 12 verses (MEASURED: web:Ezek.14.12-Ezek.14.23, tallied on the WEB face) against a 7-10 verse target length. The over-length is disclosed and carried rather than hidden: the four-scourge refrain list is never cut inside itself, and the one internal seam a reader might take, the messenger paragraph at 14:21, is weighed and held in the rejected alternative.

P03-022.boundary_rationale: Onset: 16:44 opens on the sisters' proverb of mother and daughter, הִנֵּה֙ כָּל הַמֹּשֵׁ֔ל (oshb:Ezek.16.44), and that verse carries no counted onset device - no word-event, messenger formula, son-of-man address, set-your-face command, hand-of-YHWH clause, transport verb or dateline stands in it; the plan names the cut here on content, and a naming that rests on no device licenses nothing. Its far face, MT 16:43, ends the preceding speech, but its utterance formula נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.16.43) stands mid-verse, with the lewdness clause running past it to the sof pasuq, so no verse-final close-role formula sits behind this onset either. Close: 16:58 ends verse-final on the short utterance נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.58), with a samekh recorded after that verse (single-witness), and its far face at 16:59 opens on the long messenger formula כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.16.59), which the verse-final close licenses. So the close stands two-faced while the onset's near face carries no licensed signal, and that unlicensed near face, at a seam the plan names on content, is the ground of this row's confidence. Two interior seams are weighed and held, both paragraph-grade: at 16:50/16:51 the comparison turns to Samaria after the samekh recorded on 16:50 (single-witness) and meets a verse with no onset device, and at 16:52/16:53 the restoration turn opens with no device of its own. The span runs fifteen verses against a 7-10 verse target, disclosed as a fact: this long allegory is cut only where a counted formula or the plan's own naming puts a seam.
P03-022.strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest alternative is to close at 16:50 and open a second row at 16:51, so that the Sodom comparison would stand apart from the Samaria comparison. It is weighed and not taken. On the alternative's far face the case is real - the witness records a samekh after MT 16:50 (single-witness), and the Sodom material is content-complete at that verse. On its near face it fails: MT 16:51 opens on the conjunction with Samaria, וְשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן כַּחֲצִ֥י (oshb:Ezek.16.51), the sister already named at 16:46, and MEASURED against every counted onset-formula class - word-event, messenger, son-of-man address, set-your-face, hand-of-YHWH, transport and dateline - that verse belongs to none (sweep: onset-class formulae at MT 16:51, 0 of 1 verse). A mark cannot supply the licensed onset the cut would need, so the samekh is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates while the comparison is carried on as one movement.
P03-022.device_notes: The single-witness apparatus across 16:44-16:58, disclosed in full: a Ketiv/Qere note at MT 16:47 (oshb:Ezek.16.47), where the running text reads the ketiv עשיתי in place of the Qere עָשִׂ֑ית; two such notes at MT 16:51 (oshb:Ezek.16.51) and three at MT 16:53 (oshb:Ezek.16.53), none of them used to argue this boundary; one paseq at MT 16:52 (oshb:Ezek.16.52), count-only and single-witness, with no intra-verse position claimed; an editors' note on a vowel reading at MT 16:54 (oshb:Ezek.16.54); and two parashah marks, a samekh after MT 16:50 and a samekh after MT 16:58, each single-witness. No further Ketiv/Qere note, paseq, editors' note or mark falls inside the span (sweep: 15 verses). The samekh after 16:50 is disclosed for the interior seam it corroborates rather than for this row's own edges; the one after 16:58 stands at the close. A second interior turn was weighed and not taken: the restoration named at 16:53 sits inside an ironic humiliation clause, “that you may bear your own shame” (web:Ezek.16.54), and carries no formula onset and no mark of its own.

P04-005.boundary_rationale: Every reference in this row touches the ch 20/21 numbering shift and is written dual. Onset: the strict word-event formula at web:Ezek.20.45 = oshb:Ezek.21.1 (וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר), a hard seam. MT 20:44 is followed by a pe (single-witness), corroborating the onset at MT 21:1. Close: web:Ezek.20.49 = oshb:Ezek.21.5 (וָאֹמַ֕ר אֲהָ֖הּ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הֵ֚מָּה אֹמְרִ֣ים לִ֔י הֲלֹ֛א מְמַשֵּׁ֥ל מְשָׁלִ֖ים הֽוּא), the prophet's own outcry, rendered in web:Ezek.20.49 (= oshb:Ezek.21.5) as “Isn’t he a speaker of parables”. The verse names the mashal root, but a reported taunt in the prophet's own mouth is a turn in the account and no close-role formula, so the close's near face carries no licensed signal; a pe stands immediately after it (single-witness) and corroborates that paragraph only. That unlicensed close is what this row's reduced confidence rests on. That pe is also the point where the Masoretic tradition's own paragraph division sits exactly at the WEB's chapter break, so this zone is a seam site and a numbering site at once.
P04-005.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating web:Ezek.20.45-Ezek.21.5 = oshb:Ezek.21.1-Ezek.21.10 (the mashal plus its plain-sense restatement against the land) as one row was considered and rejected: web:Ezek.21.1 = oshb:Ezek.21.6 opens with its own strict word-event formula, a second hard seam, and the outcry at web:Ezek.20.49 = oshb:Ezek.21.5 already ends the mashal, with a pe standing after it (single-witness).

P04-008.boundary_rationale: Every reference in this row touches MT ch 21. The seam references are written dual; where the weighing cites the MT face alone, it carries that face's prefix. Onset: a strict word-event formula at web:Ezek.21.8 = oshb:Ezek.21.13 (וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר), a hard seam; the verse behind it, web:Ezek.21.7 = oshb:Ezek.21.12, ends on the utterance signature, verse-final, and carries a pe after it (single-witness), so that onset is two-faced. Close: the emphatic I-YHWH-have-spoken formula at web:Ezek.21.17 = oshb:Ezek.21.22 (וְגַם אֲנִ֗י אַכֶּ֤ה כַפִּי֙ אֶל כַּפִּ֔י וַהֲנִחֹתִ֖י חֲמָתִ֑י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי), with a pe immediately after. The poem's own refrains, sharpened and polished, the sword doubled and then tripled, run between the two; the one two-faced competing onset inside them, at web:Ezek.21.14 = oshb:Ezek.21.19, is weighed below and held as a paragraph. Both outer seams are top grade on both faces -- the word-event formula against the verse-final utterance and pe behind it, and the I-YHWH-have-spoken formula with its pe against the word-event formula at web:Ezek.21.18 = oshb:Ezek.21.23 past it -- and what holds this row at medium rather than high is that interior rival, which carries real evidence on both of its own faces.
P04-008.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a second time at web:Ezek.21.12 = oshb:Ezek.21.17, which the WEB renders “Cry and wail, son of man”, was considered and rejected. That verse carries the son-of-man address, one of the 93 verses in that class, and carries no word-event and no messenger formula; the WEB opens no paragraph at it, and translation lineation would not drive a boundary in any case. A further seam was weighed one verse later, from both sides. The verse closing at web:Ezek.21.13 = oshb:Ezek.21.18 ends on the utterance formula (נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה), “says the Lord Yahweh”, with a pe following it in this witness (single-witness); the next verse, web:Ezek.21.14 = oshb:Ezek.21.19, opens with the ve'attah, the and-you address “You therefore, son of man, prophesy” (וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם הִנָּבֵ֕א). Both sides carry real evidence: an utterance-formula close on one side of the seam and, on the other, the ve'attah, an onset-class device that brings the son-of-man address with it. That signature is verse-final, its verse being one of the 81 in the long utterance class, so the second condition - the verse before it ending on a verse-final close-role formula - is met on the bytes here. What carries the unit past the seam is the shape of the renewal: a ve'attah that renews the command to prophesy to the same addressee, standing after a verse-final utterance signature, is a paragraph and not an onset. The ve'attah is new at MT 21:19, but the address it renews is not: the son-of-man address with the command to prophesy already stands at web:Ezek.21.9 = oshb:Ezek.21.14, where it introduces the book's only messenger formula naming the Lord alone, כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֑י, and the son-of-man address returns at web:Ezek.21.12 = oshb:Ezek.21.17; and MT 21:19 continues the same sword doubled a third time (וְתִכָּפֵ֞ל חֶ֤רֶב שְׁלִישִׁ֨תָה֙, oshb:Ezek.21.19), the sword already sharpened and polished at oshb:Ezek.21.14-16, rather than opening a new topic.

P06-003.boundary_rationale: Onset: 25:12 opens with the messenger formula and a fresh addressee, "כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֣עַן עֲשׂ֥וֹת אֱד֛וֹם בִּנְקֹ֥ם נָקָ֖ם לְבֵ֣ית יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֶּאְשְׁמ֥וּ אָשׁ֖וֹם וְנִקְּמ֥וּ בָהֶֽם" (oshb:Ezek.25.12) — Edom — again a messenger-formula addressee-change cut. In the WEB, “Because Edom has dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and has greatly offended, and taken revenge on them,” (web:Ezek.25.12). Close (both sides): 25:14 ends "וְנָתַתִּ֨י אֶת נִקְמָתִ֜י בֶּאֱד֗וֹם בְּיַד֙ עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעָשׂ֣וּ בֶאֱד֔וֹם כְּאַפִּ֖י וְכַחֲמָתִ֑י וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ אֶת נִקְמָתִ֔י נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.14), carrying a PE immediately after (single-witness). The close itself is a disclosed deviation from the strict recognition formula: the verb clause reads "and they shall know MY VENGEANCE" (an object noun, not "that I am YHWH"), stacked with the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature, "נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.14); it belongs to the utterance list (sweep: 81 verses), not the strict recognition list (sweep: 28 verses) or either 2ms/2mp recognition family. Behind this row, 25:11 closed Moab on the strict 3mp recognition + SAMEKH (single-witness); ahead, 25:15 opens a fresh messenger formula with the addressee change to the Philistines. Both faces of both seams therefore carry signals the witness counts; what holds this row's confidence lower is the shape of the division itself, which the plan leaves open for these oracles — four short rows, two, or one seventeen-verse row — with this row standing as one of the four.
P06-003.device_notes: 25:14's close names "my vengeance" rather than the strict "that I am YHWH" recognition object, so it is cited here as an utterance-formula close with a recognition-adjacent variant, not quoted as the strict recognition formula. A second messenger formula stands inside the span at 25:13 (oshb:Ezek.25.13), where the therefore-turn opens the verdict against Edom; it is disclosed here and licenses no seam, since the addressee does not change and 25:12 does not end on a close-role formula.

P06-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: 26:1 opens "וַיְהִ֛י בְּעַשְׁתֵּֽי עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.26.1) — a year-and-day dateline whose month is not named (“In the eleventh year, in the first of the month”, web:Ezek.26.1, WEB) together with the PERFECT-form word-event, "הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.26.1), the 7-verse hayah family the dated oracles use after their dateline, a HARD seam and the strongest onset class in the book. In the WEB, “In the eleventh year, in the first of the month, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Ezek.26.1). 26:2 supplies the accusation, "בֶּן אָדָ֗ם יַ֠עַן אֲשֶׁר אָ֨מְרָה צֹּ֤ר עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הֶאָ֔ח נִשְׁבְּרָ֛ה דַּלְת֥וֹת הָעַמִּ֖ים נָסֵ֣בָּה אֵלָ֑י אִמָּלְאָ֖ה הָחֳרָֽבָה" (oshb:Ezek.26.2), quoting Tyre's own "Aha!" against Jerusalem. Close (both sides): 26:6 ends "וּבְנוֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה בַּחֶ֖רֶב תֵּהָרַ֑גְנָה וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.26.6), the strict 3mp recognition formula, with a PE immediately after (single-witness). Ahead, 26:7 reopens with a fresh messenger formula ("כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֧י מֵבִ֣יא אֶל צֹ֗ר…", oshb:Ezek.26.7) introducing Nebuchadnezzar's siege — a new speech unit against the same addressee, not an addressee change, which is why it is held as its own row rather than folded in here: the refrain at 26:6 closes THIS unit. The onset's far face is the mid-verse recognition at 25:17 rather than a verse-final close, and the plan flags this chapter among those where onset and close collide, holding four messenger units, one row per unit, as its default, so this row's confidence stays below what its close seam alone would carry.
P06-005.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating all of 26:1-21 as one row was rejected: the chapter reads as four independently marked units (1-6, 7-14, 15-18, 19-21), the first opened by its dateline and word-event and the other three by a messenger formula, each followed by a section mark in this witness (single-witness); the 26:6 recognition-formula-plus-PE close is independently marked and, since a refrain closes the unit before it, belongs to the unit before it, forcing 26:7 to open fresh.
P06-005.device_notes: 26:1's dateline is a hard seam but not a parent seam (the oracles-against-the-nations collection is nation-ordered, not date-ordered). 26:3 carries the “Behold, I am against you” (web:Ezek.26.3, WEB) verdict-onset idiom, הִנְנִ֥י (oshb:Ezek.26.3), disclosed as sub-onset corroboration, not a competing row onset. The internal four-way split of this chapter rests on the bespoke, disclosed rationale above rather than on a forced single reading.

P06-015.boundary_rationale: Onset: 28:24 turns to Israel inside the Sidon word-event, וְלֹֽא יִהְיֶ֨ה ע֜וֹד לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Ezek.28.24), and it does so with no formula device standing in the verse - the turn is carried by its content alone. The far face behind it ends verse-final on the strict recognition formula, וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.28.23), so a counted close sits behind an onset whose own near face carries no counted signal, and that unlicensed near face is the ground of this row's confidence. Close: 28:26 ends on the recognition formula with the their-God extension, וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.28.26), verse-final in effect because only the dependent apposition follows it, and a samekh is recorded after that verse (single-witness); its far face at 29:1 opens the tenth-year dateline with the perfect-form word-event (oshb:Ezek.29.1), so the close stands two-faced. One seam inside the span is licensed on both faces and weighed rather than taken: at 28:24/28:25 the messenger formula of 28:25 (oshb:Ezek.28.25) follows 28:24's verse-final recognition and the mark after it. It is held because cutting there would leave 28:24 alone as a one-verse remainder, and because the plan names 28:24-26 as the coda to Israel - the turn to Israel, the gathering promise and the settled dwelling, one restoration movement closed by the recognition at 28:26.
P06-015.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting this coda at 28:24/28:25 instead, so that a second row would open on the messenger formula, is the strongest alternative, and it is licensed on both faces: 28:24 ends verse-final on the adonai-form recognition, וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.28.24), with a samekh recorded after that verse (single-witness), and 28:25 opens on the messenger formula כֹּֽה אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Ezek.28.25), which that verse-final close licenses. It is weighed and not taken, on two stated grounds: taking it would leave 28:24 standing alone as a one-verse remainder, and the plan names 28:24-26 as the coda to Israel, one movement - the turn to Israel, the gathering promise and the settled dwelling - closed by the recognition at 28:26. The mark is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates.
P06-015.device_notes: The single-witness apparatus inside this span: a samekh recorded after MT 28:24 (oshb:Ezek.28.24) and another after MT 28:26 (oshb:Ezek.28.26), and one paseq inside MT 28:25 (oshb:Ezek.28.25), count-only with no intra-verse position claimed. No Ketiv/Qere and no editors' note falls in the span (sweep: 3 verses). The samekh after 28:24 is disclosed for the interior seam it corroborates rather than for the onset at the head of this span. A wider alternative was weighed and refused on the plan's naming of 28:24-26 as the coda: folding these three verses back into the Sidon oracle at oshb:Ezek.28.20-Ezek.28.23 would dissolve this row's own onset seam, where MT 28:23 ends verse-final on the strict recognition formula that closes the Sidon verdict and 28:24 turns from the city to Israel's house. This coda closes the stretch of oracles against the nations that runs from chapter 25 through chapter 28 and still belongs to that collection; the next dateline seam stands outside the span at oshb:Ezek.29.1.

P10-008.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 41:12 turns to a different structure from the side-chamber circuit just closed, a change of measured object rather than a bare topic shift: וְהַבִּנְיָ֡ן אֲשֶׁר֩ אֶל פְּנֵ֨י הַגִּזְרָ֜ה פְּאַ֣ת דֶּֽרֶךְ הַיָּ֗ם (oshb:Ezek.41.12) “The building that was before the separate place at the side toward the west” (web:Ezek.41.12), confirmed by the fresh measuring verb וּמָדַ֣ד אֶת הַבַּ֔יִת (oshb:Ezek.41.13) that opens this row's own accounting of the building. The row carries the temple/separate-place/building triad each measured at a hundred cubits (41:13-14), the rear building and its galleries with a K/Q lexical variant on 'galleries' at oshb:Ezek.41.15 (ואתוקיהא, checked: a form variant, not a numeral), the side-chamber gallery structure (41:16-19), the cherubim-and-palm-tree decorative program running to above the entrance (41:18-20), the doorposts of the nave (41:21), the wooden altar-table with its own speak-formula notice, וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֚ה הַשֻּׁלְחָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.41.22), its speech rendered “This is the table that is before Yahweh” (web:Ezek.41.22), opened by the 'spoke to me' root, distinct from the 'said to me' form at 41:4, the double doors of the nave and sanctuary (41:23-25), and the repeated cherubim-and-palm-tree pattern closing on the porch threshold. Close side: 41:26 ends וְצַלְע֥וֹת הַבַּ֖יִת וְהָעֻבִּֽים (oshb:Ezek.41.26), “the side rooms of the temple and the thresholds” (web:Ezek.41.26), and the next verse, oshb:Ezek.42.1, moves the tour out to the outer court with its double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי … וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי -- a strong close by contrast, since the following onset carries the counted double-transport device even though this row's own onset rests on the measured-object change rather than a formula. P10-010.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 42:1 opens with a double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי אֶל הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה ... וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי אֶל הַלִּשְׁכָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.42.1) “he brought me out into the outer court” (web:Ezek.42.1) ... “Then he brought me into the room” (web:Ezek.42.1) -- the strongest onset in the span after 40:1 and 43:1 -- moving the tour to the priests' chambers, first north-side (42:1-9) then, by parallel description, south-side (42:10-12). Close side: 42:13-14 supplies the row's function. The guide's naming speech closes the survey of these rooms by reading and not by formula: the וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.42.13) it carries is an onset-type device inside the vision, weighed below, and no close formula at all. These are the holy chambers where the priests “eat the most holy things” (web:Ezek.42.13) and must change garments before approaching the people -- a law-toned close inside a measurement row, disclosed rather than reclassified. The double transport at the onset is a licensed onset inside the vision, a stronger opening than a bare content shift would give; the close rests on the reading above rather than on a formula, and no parashah mark stands anywhere in these chapters to corroborate either edge (single-witness).
